propositions: T5c rubric currently lacks grounding to the codebase and configuration, contradicting 46% of strong findings that cite repo artifacts and diverging from surveyed LLM security-review tools that ground exploitability in the system not the text.

T5c emits redundant undeclared-access-posture findings (one per surface) instead of capping at one finding per plan with additional surfaces folded into evidence, and 99 reviews carried ≥2 same-shape findings inflating advisory counts.

T5c ungrounded template-shape findings (30% of advisories) cannot be dropped despite being literally true, displacing other criteria in 103 advisory-cap-limited reviews; demotion to MINOR severity reduces blocking reach without suppression.

T5c must shift from advisory @ 0.95 to blocking @ 0.9 posture with rubric-text severity scoping (only two HIGH classes warrant major: plaintext secrets on boundary-crossing paths and undeclared internet-reachable sensitive surfaces) to prevent blocking via low-confidence template-shape findings.

Rubric-text edits (grounding override, dedup-at-source, demotion, two-HIGH-class scoping) implement all three behavior changes without modifying passes.py, prompts.py, or pass3_decide machinery, reusing the bfa8 T10 precedent of criterion-local severity guidance.
